finding: The displayed estimate uses M^(n+1), where M is the oscillation of the test potential. Its n integration-by-parts steps give M^n; homogeneity in the test potential requires that exponent. This item is independently identified and is not an ID from the supplied unofficial errata.
counterexample: For n=1 on the unit disc take the source test potential a=epsilon(|z|^2-1)-1, source v=|z|^2-2 and source w=-1. All are negative bounded psh, w>=v, and w-v vanishes at the boundary. M=epsilon. Put kappa=integral_disc ddc|z|^2>0. The printed left side is kappa*epsilon/3; its right side is 2*epsilon^2*integral_disc(1-|z|^2)ddc|z|^2=kappa*epsilon^2. It fails for 0<epsilon<1/3. The same example and inequality scale identically under every fixed positive ddc normalization.
repair: prop:blocki-difference-estimate proves the compact-collar form with (n+1)! M^n by exactly n substitutions, then simultaneous decreasing regularization and polynomial-weight continuity. No general zero-boundary nonsmooth integration-by-parts interface is assumed.
evidence: Smooth chain-rule estimate reconstructed; n=1 radial integrals evaluated explicitly
